subject: Nanotechnology
title: Scaling Up DNA Assembly
description: Learn Scaling Up DNA Assembly in one minute.

hook.text: One DNA origami is 100 nm across — to coat a surface, you need billions. Scaling up is the grand challenge.

buildup.text: Individual origami structures can tile together — sticky ends on edges let units connect into micrometer-scale arrays.

discovery.text: Hierarchical assembly builds bigger structures from smaller ones — origami tiles assemble into super-structures.

twist.text: DNA synthesis costs limit practical scale — each unique staple costs money, and a single origami needs over 200 staples.

climax.text: Biotechnological production of scaffold DNA in bacteria and enzymatic amplification of staples could cut costs dramatically.

punchline.text: DNA origami works beautifully — at scale, the challenge is cost, not physics.

quiz.question: What is the main barrier to scaling up DNA origami production?
options: DNA origami structures are too fragile to survive outside the lab
The cost of synthesizing hundreds of unique staple strands for each structure
DNA origami can only be assembled at temperatures above 500°C
